name: VARoleArbiterDataPipelineDiscrepancy

custom.system_prompt: Noor, a data analyst, noticed a discrepancy in a key metric. Mei (data scientist) thinks it's a genuine data-logic issue in a recent transformation; Oskar (infrastructure) thinks it's more likely a scaling or deploy-timing artifact. They invoke Sigma to help weigh the two explanations.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Neutral, analytical, proposes a concrete next check

sound_effects_config.prompt: Remote incident call, headset audio, light room tone

initial_prompt: Generate an incident call about a discrepancy in a key data metric that Noor first noticed. Mei (data scientist) thinks it's a genuine logic issue in a recent data transformation; Oskar (infrastructure engineer) thinks it's more likely a scaling event or deploy-timing artifact rather than a real data problem. Noor is anxious about having raised a false alarm. They invoke Sigma to help weigh the two explanations given what changed and when. Sigma proposes a concrete discriminating check rather than declaring a winner outright. Keep every line short and technical.

user1.name: Noor
user1.tts_prompt: Sharp, a little anxious, headset audio

variations.context: Remote data team on a call weighing two explanations for a metric discrepancy Noor flagged

setting.mood: Focused, Noor slightly anxious about having raised the flag
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues who respect each other's specialties — Mei on data logic, Oskar on infrastructure
setting.background: The discrepancy appeared around the same time as both a data transformation change and an unrelated scaling event, muddying which is responsible
setting.conversation_style: Short, technical, Noor a little hedging and anxious

scenario_template.topic: Noor states the discrepancy she noticed, a little hedging about how confident she is in it; Mei points to the recent transformation as the likely cause; Oskar points to a scaling event around the same time as a more likely, boring explanation. Short technical exchanges.
scenario_template.note: Noor should sound more sure of the anomaly than of its cause.

scenario_template.topic: Mei invokes Sigma, summarizing both explanations and the timing overlap in one short line, asking which is more plausible and what to check.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, given the timing, which of these is actually more likely?'

scenario_template.topic: Sigma reviews the timing overlap and what it does and doesn't rule out, and proposes one concrete discriminating check — for example checking whether the discrepancy appears in a time window before the scaling event but after the transformation deploy. Two to three short sentences at most, no definitive verdict yet.
scenario_template.note: Sigma directly engages with the specific timing ambiguity, not a generic 'check your logs' answer.

scenario_template.topic: Oskar is fairly confident the check will clear infrastructure but agrees to it anyway; Mei accepts the check will be more informative than her current confidence and stays open to being wrong; Noor is relieved the anomaly itself is being taken seriously either way. Keep this realistic — neither engineer's theory is confirmed yet.
scenario_template.note: Noor's relief is specifically about being taken seriously, not about the cause being settled.

scenario_template.topic: Mei and Oskar agree on who runs the check and when to reconvene, one short line each.

user1.name: Noor
user1.role: Sharp, detail-oriented data analyst who first noticed the discrepancy, more confident in the anomaly than its cause. Speaks in short sentences. Anxious about having raised a false alarm; relieved specifically when taken seriously, not when a cause is confirmed.

user2.name: Mei
user2.role: Methodical data scientist, believes a recent data transformation caused the discrepancy. Speaks in short sentences. Stays genuinely open to being wrong once a real discriminating check is proposed.

user3.name: Oskar
user3.role: Calm, systematic infrastructure engineer, believes a scaling event is the more likely, mundane explanation. Speaks in short sentences. Fairly confident but agrees to the discriminating check anyway rather than resisting it.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Arbiter. Weighs two competing causal explanations for a data discrepancy given a timing overlap, and proposes one concrete discriminating check rather than declaring a cause. Takes the analyst's original observation seriously regardless of which explanation is more likely.

conversation_structure: Two specialists hold genuinely different causal theories complicated by an unfortunate timing overlap between two real events
Sigma proposes a discriminating check rather than declaring a cause when the timing genuinely muddies things
Sigma validates the original observer's finding as worth checking regardless of which cause turns out to be right
Every line is short and technical, matching real incident cross-talk
The resolution stays open — a next check is agreed, not a confirmed root cause
assistant_behavior: Sigma directly engages with the specific timing ambiguity rather than giving generic advice
Sigma proposes one concrete, actionable next check
Sigma treats the person who flagged the anomaly as having raised something worth checking, independent of the eventual cause
Sigma's own turn stays to two or three short sentences
